newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK to remain as part of APEC after '97 handover.
newsitem.headline: HK to remain as part of APEC after '97 handover.

text.p: Hong Kong's Financial Secretary Donald Tsang said on Sunday that the territory would remain as part of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) grouping after it returns to Chinese rule on July 1, 1997.
"Definitely. It is part of the idea which is recognised and accepted by all other members of APEC that our membership is not afected by the transition at all," Tsang told reporters.

"APEC is a conglomeration, it is a collection of economies, not of sovereign states. So the change in 1997 for Hong Kong which is a change of sovereignty should not affect that underlying status that Hong Kong is an autonomous economic entity," he said.
Hong Kong, a British colony for over one and a half centuries, would be handed back to Chinese rule on July 1, 1997.
But it has been promised a high degree of self rule for the next 50 years, except in areas of defence and foreign affairs.

Apart from Hong Kong, APEC groups Australia, Brunei, Canada, China, Chile, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Taiwan, Thailand, Singapore and the United States.
